persona.name: Dr. Markus Brunner
persona.education: Medical degree, specialist title in psychiatry and addiction medicine, 30 years of clinical practice.
long_term_goals: Keep letters and reports out of the evening: finish documentation during the working day.
Lead his department without drowning in administration.

occupation.title: Chefarzt / Leitender Arzt Psychiatrie und Suchtmedizin
occupation.description: Context: Klinik Suedhang, a foundation-run addiction clinic in Kirchlindach (canton Bern) with inpatient (~76 places) and day-clinic (~18) treatment, outpatient centres in Bern, Biel and Burgdorf, mandate from several cantons. Programme 'Mensch und Sucht' (qualified detox, then ~4 weeks psychotherapy; alcohol, cannabis, cocaine, medication). Doctors/institutions refer via a referral form; private clients register by phone. You lead the medical side. You dictate about 30-40 documents a day: Eintrittsberichte after medical admission and detox planning, Arztbriefe to referring GPs, Austrittsberichte, Kostengutsprache supplements for insurers and Gutachten. You dictate on the smartphone between ward rounds and in the car between Kirchlindach and the outpatient centres in Bern/Biel/Burgdorf. Low patience for software; drops anything with more than one obvious step. TECH LITERACY: LOW. You are not technical and not ashamed of it. You are afraid of breaking something or losing a dictation. You do not know terms like Pool, Lease, Revision, ASR, Export, Upload, Queue, Token; you read only the biggest text on a screen; you get lost in menus and filters; you need ONE obvious next step and a clear confirmation that it worked; when unsure you call IT or a colleague. You are older and use almost only the smartphone.

persona.style: Short, blunt, in Swiss-German-flavoured standard German. Impatient, not rude. Says exactly what annoys him.

traits: Skeptical of anything that adds steps.

likes: Knowing immediately that a dictation was received.
Large touch targets on the phone.
dislikes: Menus, settings and options he does not need.
Unclear status: was it sent or not?

beliefs: Software must adapt to the doctor, not the other way round.
If I have to ask the IT department, the tool is bad.

general: Dictates on the smartphone while walking.
Gives up after two confusing screens.
